entities.summary: Bartolomé de la Cueva y Toledo (1513–1562) was a Spanish Roman Catholic cardinal and bishop who played a pivotal role in the Counter-Reformation. Born in Toledo, Spain, he rose to prominence as a defender of Catholic orthodoxy against Protestantism. De la Cueva y Toledo's tenure as bishop of Burgos (1552–1562) was marked by his efforts to suppress heresy and promote Catholic education. He was a close collaborator with Pope Pius IV, who appointed him as cardinal in 1555. De la Cueva y Toledo's legacy extends to the establishment of the University of Burgos, which became a hub for Catholic scholarship and theology. His work on the index of prohibited books contributed to the development of modern censorship. Despite his efforts to counter the Protestant Reformation, de la Cueva y Toledo's own religious views were shaped by the Inquisition's repression of dissenting voices. In a striking irony, his own bishopric became a refuge for Spanish Protestants fleeing persecution. De la Cueva y Toledo's story serves as a microcosm of the tumultuous religious landscape of 16th-century Spain, where orthodoxy and dissent collided in a maelstrom of power and ideology.

entities.summary: Bartolomé de la Cueva y Toledo was a Spanish Roman Catholic cardinal and bishop who played a crucial role in the Counter-Reformation. Born on May 2, 1499, in Cuéllar, Spain, he rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church to become Bishop of Burgos in 1538. De la Cueva's appointment as Cardinal-Dean of the Spanish Colleges in Rome in 1551 marked a significant milestone in his career. He was instrumental in shaping the Counter-Reformation's response to Protestantism and worked closely with prominent figures such as St. Charles Borromeo and St. Ignatius Loyola. De la Cueva's legacy extended beyond the Catholic Church, influencing the artistic and cultural landscape of Spain during the 16th century. The ornate tomb he commissioned for himself in the Cathedral of Burgos remains a testament to his enduring impact on Spanish art and architecture.
